job.task: Connect the two blue Cat5e cables from the old phone block to new keystone jacks, join them with a patch cord, then test the link
job.job_title: Terminate two Cat5e cables to keystone jacks
tools_needed: 110-style punch-down tool (a small hand tool that pushes wire into a slot and trims the end in one push)
Cat5e keystone jack × 2 (the small snap-in data socket the patch cord plugs into)
Keystone-compatible surface or panel mount / faceplate to hold the jacks
Cat5e patch cord (a short pre-made cable with RJ-45 plugs on both ends)
Cable tester (a cheap two-piece unit that lights LEDs to confirm each wire is connected)

step.title: Identify the two blue Cat5e cables
step.action: Look at the existing phone distribution block (the black strip with coloured wire slots visible in the centre of the panel) and locate the two blue Cat5e cables currently punched into it. Put a small piece of masking tape on each one and label them 'A' and 'B' so you never confuse them.
do_not_touch: coax splitter and coax cables at the top of the panel
yellow-green ground wire at the bottom
black thick cables on the right
step.stop_condition: If either cable feels warm or you see any scorch marks near where the cable enters the block, stop and contact a licensed technician.
step.evidence_required: Photo showing both blue cables with visible 'A' and 'B' labels attached.

verdict.reason: Blue cables are visible but there are no masking tape labels marked 'A' or 'B' attached to either of them.
